title: kernel-reservoir-and-dequant-amplifier-for-mixed-precision-handoffs
creator: Priya Rao
description: Problem: When routing between INT8 and FP8 execution paths we observe spiky decode latency due to synchronous dequant steps and contention on a small set of optimized kernels. This ticket proposes a kernel reservoir + dequant amplifier approach: a lightweight reservation layer that pre-allocates a small pool of quantization-friendly kernel instances and applies a calibrated fractional-cast 'amplifier' during prefill to smooth latency outliers without regressing token throughput or output quality. Goals: 1) reduce P99 decode latency variance by 20-30% for mixed workloads, 2) keep mean token cost change < 5%, 3) provide hooks for runtime telemetry to attribute latency to dequant amplification and reservoir pressure.
acceptance_criteria: Add kernel reservoir manager that can reserve up to N lightweight kernel slots per GPU and expose pressure signals via runtime telemetry
Implement fractional-cast dequant amplifier applied during prefill to reduce synchronous dequant stalls; feature gated and toggleable per model/route
End-to-end microbench shows P99 decode latency improvement >= 20% on mixed INT8/FP8 workload (baseline: current runtime main branch)
No output-regression: evaluation on 2 representative prompt suites shows quality delta within configured tolerance (ROUGE/EM thresholds)
Config knobs surfaced in Console: reservoir_size, amplifier_strength, prefill_threshold, and grace_window
Automated integration tests and a perf CI job added that measures reservoir pressure and amplifier latency cost
tasks: Design: document kernel reservoir state machine and reservation policy (concurrency, steal, fallback)
Prototype: implement reservoir manager and minimal slot lifecycle in runtime core (C++/CUDA)
Algorithm: implement fractional-cast amplifier (adaptive strength based on recent dequant latency) in prefill pipeline
Benchmarks: create microbench harness for mixed-precision prefill/streaming with synthetic head-length distributions
Telemetry: add tracer spans and metrics (reservoir_in_use, amplifier_applied, dequant_sync_ms)
Console: add a per-route toggle and runtime dashboard for reservoir pressure and amplifier effect
Docs & rollout: PRD update, ops runbook, rollback plan and feature flag default off for 48h canary
comments: 2026-02-26 Priya Rao: Triaged after perf spike incident on 2026-02-25. Root cause appears to be bursty dequant calls plus kernel warmup thrash on a narrow set of optimized kernels.

2026-03-02 Jordan Kim: PoC reservoir manager implemented. Basic API: reserve_slot(route_id) returns slot token or null. Observed ~15% P95 improvement in single-GPU synthetic runs but P99 unchanged. Investigating amplifier parameters.

2026-03-04 Miguel Ortega (review): Suggest using a leaky-bucket style refill for reservoir instead of simple time-based reset to avoid synchronized refills across workers. Also: ensure slots are cheap (no heavyweight CUDA context work) or else reservoir will worsen contention.

2026-03-06 Jordan Kim: Integrated fractional-cast amplifier into prefill path. The amplifier applies a partial dequant transform that defers full-width dequant until decode steady-state. Initial tuning: amplifier_strength=0.4 reduces median dequant_sync_ms by ~30ms at cost of +2% token compute. Still running longer runs for P99.

2026-03-09 Ops note (Sven Müller): Canary on dedicated cluster (dev-dedicated-2) for 12h. Observed two small regressions correlated with reservoir exhaustion when many small routes hit simultaneously; added graceful fallback to force immediate full dequant if amplifier backlog exceeds 3x reservoir_size.

2026-03-12 Priya Rao: Design review with Product and Console teams. Action items: (1) surface reservoir pressure metric to alerts, (2) add per-customer default reservoir caps to avoid noisy tenants, (3) run quality evals on long-context code generation prompts. Assigned follow-ups to ENG-100438 (quality eval harness) and PM-412 (pricing/limits review).
